newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: PIHP says hotels all profitable.
newsitem.headline: PIHP says hotels all profitable.

text.p: Pernas International Holdings Bhd (PIHP) said on Monday that all 11 hotels now in its stable are profitable and it was not worried about an oversupply of hotel rooms.

PIHP, formerly Pernas International Hotels and Properties, became Malaysia's biggest hotel operator when the assets of the government's investment holding company Perbadanan Nasional Bhd were injected into it last week.
From three hotels previously, the company now has 11 with two more on the drawing board, PIHP deputy general manager Mohamed Khadar Merican told a media and analysts' briefing.
Mohamed said all of the hotels, including those under Pernas's previous management, had reported operating profits last year.
But in reply to a question, he said the division as a whole had reported a pre-tax loss due to "undercapitalisation of the hotels and interest charges." He did not elaborate.
Senior managers from Pernas took a controlling 32 percent stake in PIHP after the Pernas asset injection last week in Malaysia's biggest ever management buyout.
Asked about worries that Malaysia would have a glut of hotel rooms after 1998, Mohamed said: "We think the demand will be there. The new airport will increase arrivals."
He said that despite escalating competition, "all of our hotels have maintained their market share."
The hotel industry has seen a building spurt to accommodate visitors to the 1998 Commonwealth Games, which Malaysia hosts.

A nine-billion-ringgit ($3.6 billion) airport, also due to open in 1998, is designed to become a regional hub able to accommodate many more flights than the current international airport in Kuala Lumpur.
Mohamed said among the most profitable hotels in the PIHP chain were the Istana in Kuala Lumpur and two Langkawi beach resorts, Pelangi and Bureau Bay.

Among the least profitable were two eco-tourism ventures -- Taman Negara in a national park in Peninsular Malaysia and the newly-opened Batang Ai resort in the remote interior of the Borneo state of Sarawak.

Three Hilton hotels and one Holiday Inn are also part of the chain. Mohamed said the company planned to open new hotels in the southern state of Johor and in Kota Kinabalu, the capital of the north Borneo state of Sabah.
